mechanicalValidation.verdict: The class/code table is internally consistent, but the golden format is not yet a conformance fixture for HostTermination because twelve cases omit fields their selected union variant declares required.

peerDecisionResponses.reasoning: A serve process that receives SIGINT/SIGTERM and actually completes cooperative protocol and resource cleanup has fulfilled its lifecycle and exits success/0. Forced or failed shutdown is not this case.
latest is a single-identity resolver, not a collection query. An empty domain cannot satisfy the request and returns request-rejected/2 with RESOLVER.EMPTY_DOMAIN.
Indeterminate/3 is the correct termination, but class/code alone does not encode C4/F3's stronger guarantee that comparison is not performed and no synthetic net-new findings are emitted.
peerDecisionResponses.requiredRefinement: The golden must assert zero comparison-derived findings, fingerprint-recipe-unsupported, and a previewable upgrade/legacy-support repair action.

peerDecisionResponses.reasoning: Back-references are necessary, but a list of self-asserted prose cannot prove coverage and currently conflates properties this artifact assumes with properties it tests.
peerDecisionResponses.requiredRefinement: Use stable decision IDs and map each conformance claim to existing golden/invariant IDs; list mere dependencies separately.

findings.title: The golden cases are classification examples, not union-conforming HostTermination fixtures
findings.detail: v1.1 declares required payload per union variant, then omits that payload from twelve selected cases. The current jq proof only validates class-to-code mapping, so an implementation could omit runId, errorCode, reasonCodes, or signal and still satisfy every mechanical check.
findings.requiredFix: Replace expectedClass/expectedCode plus ad-hoc sibling fields with expectedTermination objects validated by a JSON Schema. Fixture references such as $RUN_ID are acceptable, but every variant-required field must be present.

findings.title: The baseline golden still does not enforce the no-mass-false-net-new property it claims to cover
findings.detail: baseline-compare-unsupported-recipe asserts only indeterminate/3. A conforming implementation could still emit thousands of comparison-derived findings and then exit 3. That remains the C4/F3 trust failure, only with a different exit code.
findings.requiredFix: Add expectedEffects with comparisonPerformed=false, comparisonDerivedFindingCount=0, and repair action baseline-upgrade-preview or supported-legacy-match.

findings.title: Interruption precedence has no finalization linearization point
findings.detail: The first analysis rule maps any user signal to interrupted. A signal arriving after a Run and required postconditions completed but before process exit can race a settled pass/fail into 130. Exit then depends on scheduling rather than command semantics.
findings.requiredFix: Define a cancellability/finalization commit point. Signals accepted before it may derive interrupted; signals after it request transport shutdown but cannot reclassify the settled HostTermination. Required output/delivery postconditions occur before the commit point.

findings.title: sealedPropertiesCovered is self-attestation rather than traceable conformance
findings.detail: The free-text array says this D9 artifact covers C5 multi-process safety and item 38 policy ownership, but D9 only classifies a busy-timeout and assumes project-owned policy; it does not prove either property. This recreates the exact silent-drop risk the field was meant to prevent.
findings.requiredFix: Split decisionDependencies from conformanceClaims. Each claim uses a stable decision/ADR ID, names the scoped obligation, and references concrete golden/invariant IDs. Review rejects dangling IDs and unsupported coverage claims.

findings.title: IDENTITY.EXPIRED versus NEVER_EXISTED requires storage evidence
findings.detail: Once a Run is retention-collected, absence from the live ledger cannot by itself prove it expired rather than never existed. Emitting the more specific code without a retained tombstone would manufacture provenance.
findings.requiredFix: D3 retains a minimal RunId tombstone sufficient to prove expiry, or the resolver emits IDENTITY.UNKNOWN when it cannot distinguish. Add the storage precondition to the error-code definition.

d1Item38LockAuthority.detail: The A3/A1 instruction to put effective severity mapping in opensip.lock conflicts with item 38 and D13: project intent owns policy, while the lock pins contribution/artifact resolution separately from intent. Making a generated lockfile authoritative for severity moves policy back out of reviewed intent.
d1Item38LockAuthority.requiredRule: Tracked project policy stores effective severity/gate mapping or selects a versioned project-owned PolicyProfile. opensip.lock stores contribution digests and may record the resolved-policy digest/default provenance for reproducibility, but it is not the policy source of truth. An extension recommendation change produces a previewable policy diff and requires explicit acceptance.

d5SchemaIdentity.rule: CommandEnvelope uses a distinct schema-family ID plus major negotiation and dual projection; D9 is a component of that wire contract, not an independent sixth public contract.

d19Slice1.rule: Internal parity adapters may proceed; public ProjectDescriptor, ResolvedConfig, and envelope ABI remain unfrozen pending their artifacts.

requiredV12Changes: Introduce a JSON Schema for the artifact and expectedTermination fixtures; fill all variant-required payloads.
Strengthen the unsupported-recipe case with no-comparison/no-derived-findings effects and repair metadata.
Add a finalization commit-point invariant and at least one post-commit-signal golden.
Replace free-text sealedPropertiesCovered with stable decisionDependencies plus evidence-linked conformanceClaims.
State the tombstone/IDENTITY.UNKNOWN requirement for expiry classification.
Keep the four peer decisions merged as classified above.
overall: HostTermination and all four referred classifications are accepted. v1.1 is not yet implementation-binding because its goldens do not conform to its own union, its C4/F3 claim checks only the exit and not the prohibited effects, and its sealed-property back-references are not auditable. Merge the required v1.2 changes, then run the schema validator and executable mapper goldens before sealing D9.
